# Ed25519 reference fixtures

`cctv-dalek-1.0.1.json` contains the 914 original [CCTV Ed25519 vectors](https://github.com/C2SP/CCTV/tree/main/ed25519), with `dalek_strict` added by the pinned oracle. The original corpus hash is in `provenance.json`; its license is `CCTV-LICENSE`. 43 cases pass the Solana precompile's exact `ed25519-dalek 1.0.1`/`curve25519-dalek 3.2.0` predicate.

`scalars-dalek-4.1.3.json` uses the basepoint plus each of the eight torsion classes. Its 320 cases cover 0,1,2,3,L−1,L−2,L−3 and powers-of-two boundaries. `r_for_s5` is `[5]B−[h]A`, generated by Rust; the Go tests use it to check the entire short verification equation for a supplied challenge, including h=0 and mixed torsion. The fixed-base tests use its 40 torsion-free rows. The supplied-challenge tests also use `result` to check zero S at h=1 and reject identity R at h=0 across all eight torsion classes.

Both files come from a pinned Rust oracle crate that is not part of this repository; it lives in the zk-experiments repository at `gnark-gadgets/ed25519/testdata/oracle`. Regenerate there, outside the production Go dependency graph, and copy the outputs here:

```sh
cargo run --locked --release --manifest-path ed25519/testdata/oracle/Cargo.toml --bin cctv -- /path/to/original/ed25519vectors.json > ed25519/testdata/cctv-dalek-1.0.1.json
cargo run --locked --release --manifest-path ed25519/testdata/oracle/Cargo.toml --bin scalars > ed25519/testdata/scalars-dalek-4.1.3.json
```

The Solana version pin comes from [Agave's precompile manifest](https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/master/precompiles/Cargo.toml) and [lockfile](https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/master/Cargo.lock). Its [`verify_strict`](https://github.com/dalek-cryptography/ed25519-dalek/blob/1.0.1/src/public.rs) compares decoded R points, permitting noncanonical point encodings. The message hash always uses the original encoded bytes.
